title: Choosing among population-adjustment models on the same data
question: When the adjustment model is chosen from the analyzed data, does the chosen model's interval keep its coverage, and what does averaging over candidates change?
design: Re-scoring of DIA-08's stored replicates (16 scenarios x 2000) under prespecified, precision-selected, result-selected and averaged use of four adjustment methods.
answer: For choices among MAIC and STC specifications the candidates are close: choosing the most precise method covered 0.938 to 0.956, like a prespecified one. Choosing the most favorable estimate shifted it by up to 0.26 on the log odds ratio scale while its interval still covered 0.927 or more, because the favored method often had a wide interval. Averaging with between-model variance over-covered (up to 0.991) because the candidates share data; that difference makes the refuting sentence fail as registered.
findings: Registered verdict FAILS, through the averaged interval's coverage differing from the prespecified one's by more than 0.03.
Selection by smallest SE: coverage 0.938 to 0.956, bias as the prespecified linear STC.
Selection by most favorable estimate: bias -0.046 to -0.259, coverage 0.927 to 0.960.
Equal-weight average with added between-model variance: coverage 0.949 to 0.991, the widest intervals.
not_answered: Outcome and weighting models only; treatment partitions and bridges not studied; equal weights. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target (DIA-08)
